chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Al-Hajjaj, who said:

I bought a loader, so I gave part of its price and left it with its owner. Then I was detained for a few days, then I came to the seller of the loader to take it, so he said, 'I have sold it.' So I laughed, then I said, 'No, by Allah, I will not let you go, or I will seek judgment against you.' So he said to me, 'Would you be pleased with Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash?' I said, 'Yes.' So we went to him and related our story to him. So Abu Bakr said, 'By whose words do you like that I judge between the two of you, by the words of your companion or someone else?' He said, 'I said, by the words of my companion.' He said, 'I heard him saying: Whoever buys something and brings the price within what is between it and three days, otherwise there is no sale for him.'

key_terms.أُقَاضِيَكَ: I will seek judgment/adjudication from you
key_terms.فِي مَا بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَ ثَلَاثَةِ أَيَ: Within the period between now and three days

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a sale where the buyer pays part of the price and has a few days to pay the rest?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated via the chain of Safwan ibn Yahya, establishes the 'khiyar al-shart' (option of condition) in sales, specifically limiting the buyer's right to cancel to a three-day period after partial payment. Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash, a prominent early jurist, validates this by citing the Prophet’s tradition that a sale is not final if the full price is not settled within three days, highlighting the Shia emphasis on contractual clarity and the prevention of uncertainty (gharar) in commercial transactions.
